q: An officer is appointed to a post on the condition that he may hold it only for a limited term, even though the post itself is permanent in nature. Such a post is classified under the Fundamental Rules as a:

options.A: A permanent post which an individual railway servant may not ordinarily hold for more than a limited period
options.B: A post held by a railway servant during his period of probation
options.C: A temporary post sanctioned for a work of short duration
options.D: A post from which a railway servant can be removed at any time without notice

q: For establishment purposes, the sanctioned strength of a service, or of a distinct part of a service treated as a separate unit, is referred to in the Fundamental Rules as its:

options.A: The seniority list of a service
options.B: The strength of a service, or a part of a service, sanctioned as a separate unit
options.C: The total number of employees working in an office at a given time
options.D: A group of officers recruited to a service in the same year

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 8 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 38,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:

A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 38,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent of basic pay. The monthly contribution payable by the railway servant himself to his Tier-I account, at 10 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:

The pay of a gazetted railway servant in an office is drawn by the establishment on the basis of an authority issued for the purpose showing the pay and allowances admissible to him. That authority, the pay slip, is issued by:

options.B: The Railway Recruitment Board
options.C: The recognised officers' association of the Railway
options.D: The gazetted railway servant himself, by self-declaration

q: A claim for arrears of pay and allowances of a railway servant is not preferred within one year of the date on which it became due. Before such a claim can be paid, it is required to be subjected to:

options.A: A vigilance inquiry by the Vigilance Department
options.B: Pre-audit by the Accounts Office, in accordance with the rules for investigation of arrear claims
options.C: The approval of the Railway Board in every case
options.D: An inquiry by the Central Administrative Tribunal

q: The pay for a month has already been disbursed, and arrears for an earlier period thereafter become payable to a clerk because of a retrospective pay fixation order. These arrears are claimed by the establishment through:

options.A: A supplementary pay bill prepared for the purpose
options.B: The travelling allowance bill of the railway servant
options.C: The contingent bill of the office
options.D: A fresh appointment order issued by the competent authority

q: The statement attached to a supplementary pay bill, setting out in respect of each railway servant the amount of pay and allowances due to him, the amount already drawn by him and the net amount now claimed, is known as the:

options.B: Increment certificate
options.C: Last Pay Certificate
options.D: Due-drawn statement

q: In addition to the Head of Office verifying and attesting the entries in a Service Book every year, the rules also require that:

options.A: It is sent to the Accounts Office every year for safe custody
options.B: It is shown to the railway servant concerned every year and his signature obtained in it in token of his having seen it
options.C: It is shown to the railway servant only at the time of his retirement
options.D: It is rewritten afresh every five years by the office

q: The original Service Book of a railway servant is lost in his office. In regard to the record of his service, the correct position is that:

options.A: A fresh service record is started from the date of loss, ignoring the earlier service
options.B: The railway servant is treated as a fresh entrant for all purposes
options.C: A duplicate Service Book may be prepared by the Head of Office on the basis of the available records, the past entries being verified and reconstructed as far as possible
options.D: No duplicate Service Book can be prepared under any circumstances

q: A doubt arises in a divisional office about who keeps the leave account of a non-gazetted clerk serving in that office. The account is kept:

options.A: By the Accounts Office which checks his pay bills
options.B: By the pension section of the zonal railway headquarters
options.C: In the prescribed form, along with his Service Book, by the office in which he is serving
options.D: By the office of the General Manager of the zonal railway

q: The leave account of a railway servant is lost and is not available in his office. In such a case, the leave account is reconstructed:

options.A: On the basis of available collateral records, such as pay bills, absentee statements and the entries in his Service Book
options.B: By crediting him with 300 days of Leave on Average Pay in all cases
options.C: Only from the date of the loss, ignoring the leave availed of by him earlier
options.D: Solely on the basis of a declaration made by the railway servant himself

q: A railway servant applies, after availing a spell of leave, for its conversion into another kind of leave. Such conversion by the leave sanctioning authority is permissible provided that:

options.A: The railway servant refunds the whole of the leave salary already drawn by him
options.B: The other kind of leave was due and admissible to him at the time the leave originally granted was availed of
options.C: The Railway Board sanctions the conversion in every case
options.D: The conversion is sought only within one year before his retirement
